pageInfo.subtitle: Develop precise timing, groove, and rhythmic accuracy with essential strumming and timing exercises.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Rhythm is the heartbeat of music. These exercises will help you develop solid timing, consistent strumming patterns, and the ability to play with precision and groove. Master these fundamentals to become a confident rhythm guitarist and ensemble player.

items.text: Start slowly and gradually increase tempo
Focus on consistent, even strumming motion
Count out loud or tap your foot
Keep your strumming arm relaxed and fluid
Use wrist motion more than arm motion
Practice ghost strums for complex patterns

exercises.title: Quarter Note Strumming
exercises.description: Master the foundation of rhythm guitar with steady quarter note strumming. This exercise develops consistent timing and forms the basis for all other strumming patterns.

patternNote.text: Pattern: Down - Down - Down - Down (on beats 1, 2, 3, 4)

notation.title: Quarter Note Strumming Exercise
notation.staveTitle: C Major Chord - Quarter Note Strums

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use all downstrokes and focus on hitting the strings at exactly the same time as the metronome click. Keep your strumming motion consistent and relaxed. Count "1, 2, 3, 4" out loud.

exercises.title: Basic Down-Up Strumming
exercises.description: Introduce eighth note patterns with alternating down and up strokes. This is the foundation of most popular music strumming patterns.

notation.title: Basic Down-Up Strumming Exercise
notation.staveTitle: C Major Chord - Eighth Note Down-Up Pattern

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Alternate between downstrokes and upstrokes. Keep your hand moving in steady eighth note motion even when not hitting strings. Count "1-and-2-and-3-and-4-and".

exercises.title: Popular "Down-Down-Up-Up-Down-Up" Pattern
exercises.description: Learn one of the most common strumming patterns in popular music. This pattern appears in countless songs across multiple genres.

patternNote.text: D-D-U-U-D-U (Down on 1, Down on 2, Up on 2+, Up on 3+, Down on 4, Up on 4+)

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: This pattern creates a great groove for folk, pop, and rock songs. Focus on the syncopated upstrokes and maintain steady hand motion throughout. Practice slowly before attempting full speed.

exercises.title: Syncopated Rhythm Pattern
exercises.description: Master syncopation with this off-beat emphasis pattern. Syncopation adds groove and sophistication to your rhythm playing.

notation.title: Syncopated Rhythm Exercise
notation.staveTitle: E Minor Chord - Syncopated Pattern with Muted Strums

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Practice ghost strums (muted upstrokes) on beats 2 and 4. Keep your hand moving continuously but dampen the strings with your fretting hand during the ghost strums.

exercises.title: Reggae Skank Pattern
exercises.description: Learn the classic reggae "skank" rhythm with emphasis on the off-beats. This pattern is fundamental to reggae, ska, and related Caribbean styles.

notation.title: Reggae Skank Exercise
notation.staveTitle: A Minor Chord - Reggae Skank Pattern

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Emphasize the upstrokes on the off-beats (the "and" counts). Use short, staccato chords with palm muting for an authentic reggae sound. Keep the rhythm very steady.

exercises.title: Complex 16th Note Pattern
exercises.description: Challenge yourself with intricate 16th note patterns that combine downstrokes, upstrokes, and ghost strums for complex rhythmic textures.

notation.title: Complex 16th Note Exercise
notation.staveTitle: D Major Chord - Complex 16th Note Pattern

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: This advanced pattern requires precise timing and coordination. Practice very slowly first, counting 16th notes: "1-e-and-a-2-e-and-a-3-e-and-a-4-e-and-a". Build speed gradually.

exercises.title: Metronome Training Exercises
exercises.description: Develop rock-solid timing with these metronome-based exercises that challenge your internal clock and rhythmic precision. Progressive Timing Drills: Click on 1 - Metronome only on beat 1, you provide beats 2, 3, 4. Click on 1 & 3 - Metronome on strong beats, you fill weak beats. Click on 2 & 4 - Metronome on backbeat only. Half-time click - Metronome at half speed, play double-time. Off-beat click - Metronome on off-beats only. Random drops - Metronome cuts out randomly, maintain tempo.

items.title: Technique Focus
items: Keep your strumming arm relaxed and use wrist motion
Maintain consistent hand motion even during rests
Count out loud to internalize complex patterns
Practice slowly with metronome before increasing tempo

items.title: Why Rhythm Matters
items: Rhythm is the foundation that holds music together
Strong rhythmic skills make you a valuable ensemble player and allow you to communicate musically with other musicians
Whether playing solo or in a band, solid rhythm and timing create the groove that makes people want to move and feel the music
These skills translate to all styles and instruments
